heroSummary: The Bambu Lab X1C handles Polymaker PolyTerra PLA exceptionally well out of the box, reaching safe print speeds up to 250 mm/s based on its 21 mm³/s maximum volumetric flow rate. Keep the glass top or front door vented to avoid heat creep during prolonged prints within the enclosed chamber.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with no adhesive required (clean with isopropyl alcohol or warm dish soap).
slicerTweaks: Set the Maximum Volumetric Speed limit to 21 mm³/s in the filament profile to prevent underextrusion at high speeds.
Tune Pressure Advance (Linear Advance) specifically between 0.022 and 0.028 to maintain sharp corners and prevent matte surface bulging.
Keep Chamber Temperature Management in check by venting the top glass lid or setting the chamber exhaust fan to 70% to prevent heat creep.
Lower outer wall speed to 120-150 mm/s while keeping inner walls at 250 mm/s to ensure an ultra-uniform matte surface finish.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Extruder clicking and clogs during long prints
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Heat creep caused by printing low-temperature PLA inside a fully sealed X1C chamber, softening the filament above the heat break.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Prop open the top glass cover or crack the front glass door during printing, and verify the cold-end fan is running at 100%.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Weak layer adhesion and brittle parts along Z-axis
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive high-speed part cooling combined with printing below the optimal polymer bonding temperature for matte PLA.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Increase nozzle temperature from 210°C to 220°C and reduce the auxiliary part cooling fan to 30% or turn it off entirely.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Uneven matte sheen and patchy striping on outer perimeters
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Speed differential between standard wall paths and decelerations causing localized cooling rate variations.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Enable 'Precise Z-height' and set a uniform outer wall speed (e.g., 100-120 mm/s) so melt temperature and cooling stay consistent.

faq.question: Can I print Polymaker PolyTerra PLA directly from the Bambu AMS?
faq.answer: Yes, PolyTerra PLA is compatible with the AMS; however, ensure the cardboard spool edges are in good condition or use printable spool rim adapters to prevent cardboard dust and rotation slipping.

faq.question: Do I need glue stick on the Bambu Textured PEI plate for PolyTerra PLA?
faq.answer: No, PolyTerra PLA adheres exceptionally well to a clean Textured PEI plate at 55°C without any glue or adhesive aids and releases naturally once cooled.

faq.question: Why is the top surface rougher than standard PLA at high speeds?
faq.answer: PolyTerra contains organic/mineral matte additives that make the melt less fluid; lower your top surface speed to 80 mm/s and enable ironing for a smooth velvety finish.

faq.question: Do I need to dry PolyTerra PLA before printing on the X1C?
faq.answer: While not strongly hygroscopic like nylon, fresh or moist spools can show mild stringing; drying at 45°C for 4-6 hours restores optimal string-free performance.
